utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is IT-09-92-PT, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Mr. Mladic, would you be so kind to take off your cap. If you take off your hat then it's easier to listen.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: No microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, could you ask Mr. Mladic to remain silent for a second. Mr. Lukic, if Mr. Mladic talks to you, if it's a confidential communication between counsel and his client, then he should whisper rather than to speak aloud. If he wants to address the Court, he can do so through you, and then of course we need a microphone switched on, otherwise we'll not hear what he's addressed. I asked Mr. Mladic to take off his hat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is Mr. Mladic willing to take off his hat?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. -- Mr. Lukic, could you -- Mr. Lukic, could you tell Mr. Mladic that my patience is limited and that he's hereby invited to take off his hat. Thank you. Please be seated, Mr. Mladic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mladic, if you want to speak to counsel, do it, please, in such a way that not everyone is hearing it, because that is considered to be confidential. Please be seated and then I'll start with the appearances. Appearances. Prosecution first.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. For the Prosecution, Dermot Groome, Peter McCloskey, Roeland Bos, and Janet Stewart.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Groome. For the Defence, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Branko Lukic and Milos Saljic for the Defence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic. And we see that the -- Mr. Mladic, the accused, is present. I see that Mr. Mladic is again, as he did before, seeking to communicate by his body language and gestures with the public gallery. Now, we have a public gallery because these are public proceedings, not to allow Mr. Mladic to communicate in an uncontrolled way even without speaking with the public gallery. So therefore, Mr. Mladic, either you now refrain from eye contact, gestures, et cetera, with the public gallery, because otherwise we have to put a screen between you and the public gallery so that everyone still can see you through the cameras but that you're not able anymore to communicate in the way you did a minute ago, and you did before, to use the public gallery for your own purposes. Is that clear? Today a Status Conference has been scheduled. Now, before this Status Conference, the Chamber will hold a Further Appearance for the accused to enter a plea to the new charge contained in the now operative Third Amended Indictment. This Further Initial Appearance was originally scheduled for the last Status Conference, of the 10th of November, but due to Mr. Mladic's absence from court the Further Appearance was postponed. The Chamber had considered rescheduling the future appearance for the 24th of November of this year and inquired with the United Nations Detention Unit as to whether Mr. Mladic's health had improved enough for him to attend such a proceeding. On the 19th of November, the Chamber received a courtesy copy of the UNDU reporting medical officer report, indicating that Mr. Mladic's current health condition had improved to the point that he would be able to attend court proceedings. This report was formally filed on the 22nd of November. However, after the Chamber was informed of scheduling conflicts for the parties, the Chamber ultimately determined not to move forward with the 24th of November date. And subsequently, the Further Appearance was rescheduled for today's Status Conference. On the 20th of October, 2011, the Prosecution filed the Third Amended Indictment, adding a new incident, the Bisina incident, and making technical corrections to the names of several locations and persons listed in the indictment schedules. These technical corrections consist mainly of adding diacritics and previously omitted letters in the names of certain municipalities and persons. The Chamber has reviewed these corrections and accepts that they make no substantive changes to the indictment. I now move on to the plea to the new charge in the Third Amended Indictment. On the 13th of October, the Chamber issued its decision on the consolidated Prosecution motion to sever the indictment, conduct separate trials, and to amend the indictment. In its decision, the Chamber found that amending the Second Amended Indictment to include the Bisina incident would result in a new charge and ordered that a Further Appearance be held following the filing of the Third Amended Indictment to enable the accused to enter a plea on the new charge. As I stated already, the Third Amended Indictment was filed on the 20th of October, 2011. Schedule E, part 1 of the Third Amended Indictment titled "Srebrenica Killings," "Organised Killings," now includes the following incident, listed as Incident 12, and I quote: "Location - Bisina: The killing of over thirty Bosnian Muslim men, some of whom were previously detained in Susica prison, in Bisina in Sekovici municipality. Date: 23rd of July, 1995." The Bisina incident constitutes a new basis for conviction of the accused under the Third Amended Indictment on the Counts 2, which deals with genocide; Count 3, which deals with persecution as a crime against humanity; Count 4, which deals with extermination as a crime against humanity; Count 5, which deals with murder as a crime against humanity; and Count 6, which deals with murder as a war crime. Mr. Mladic, a not guilty plea was entered on your behalf to these counts at the Further Appearance of the 4th of July, 2011. My question to you is: Do you wish for that not guilty plea to extend to the new Bisina charges as it applies to these counts, or do you wish to enter a plea on each count in relation to the Bisina charges? So do you want to extend your not guilty plea to the Bisina charges or do you want to enter a specific plea on Counts 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6 in relation to that Bisina charge? What do you prefer?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- I offer my help, and I would -- Mr. Mladic just informed me that he enters not guilty plea on these -- on Bisina charge as well. It would -- he wants to have transcript in Serbian. I am trying to explain him that it's not possible, but he says that he follows you pretty hard only through audio because he thinks -- he says that he's very slow so he -- and you talk fast. So it's hard for him to follow you only verbally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If at any moment Mr. Mladic would like me to slow down, I'll be glad to do so. And perhaps I put it in rather simple terms to him again. Mr. Mladic, you are expected to enter a plea. The Bisina incident is now part of Counts 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6. You have entered a not guilty plea to those counts or, I should say, a not guilty plea has been entered on your behalf to these counts. Do you now want to extend that plea of not guilty also to the Bisina charge? If that is what you wish to do, please tell me.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, you said this slowly, and I'm not clear what Bisina means as a term. Is that a mountain? Is that a river? Is that a brook? Is that some kind of bridge? Is it a movable feature such as a bus, truck, plane, helicopter? What is Bisina? You're mentioning Sekovici; I know what Sekovici is. But I don't know what Bisina is. Is that some kind of place or is it a village? What is it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is a location in Sekovici municipality, where - and that's the charge brought against you - that over 30 Bosnian Muslim men were killed, men some of whom had previously been detained in Susica prison. And it is charged to have happened on the 23rd of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for this explanation. I'm not guilty and I have nothing whatsoever to do with it, not with the date, not with the place, not with Bisina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then it's hereby on the record that the not guilty plea on Counts 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6 extends to Incident 12 of Schedule E, part 1, of the Third Amended Indictment, which refers to the killing of over 30 Bosnian Muslim men in Bisina. Therefore, your not guilty plea is hereby on the record. In accordance with the procedures of Rule 50(C), the Defence has 30 days from the entering of these pleas, that is, of today, to file any Rule 72 preliminary motions related to this new charge. Mr. Lukic, could you already now indicate whether the Defence intends to file such a motion?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I have to see with my whole team and with the client, but I do not envisage filing of a separate motion on this incident.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But I will probably inform the Court in the next five days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We are awaiting any further news about your intentions in this respect. Now, the Chamber will now have a recess of 30 minutes to allow the audio/visual staff time to finish their preparations for the Status Conference broadcast, and therefore we'll have a break and we'll resume at five minutes to 5.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: adjourned at 4.24 p.m. 24 25
